proposed_comments.title: Keep deferred release failures synchronized with engine state

confidence.rationale: PostThreadMessageW reports only queueing, while the engine immediately commits release state; the current deferred SendInput failure is discarded.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep deferred release failures synchronized with engine state

**Severity:** `high`

`PostThreadMessageW` succeeding only means the release request was queued, but the engine treats that result as if `SendInput` already succeeded. If the deferred injection fails, a same-button release can swallow both physical events or a settings/lifecycle release can clear the logical lock while Windows still sees the button held. Report deferred completion back to the engine, distinguish the same-button paired-up path from other releases, and add regression tests that prove failure either lets the physical up through or restores the logical lock.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This concern requires coordinated changes across multiple current-diff regions or files, so it cannot be safely expressed as one apply-ready inline suggestion.

proposed_comments.title: Avoid injecting a global Escape during right-button release

confidence.rationale: The code unconditionally injects Escape after non-chorded right-button releases without proving that a context menu opened or that modifiers are not held.

proposed_comments.body:
### Avoid injecting a global Escape during right-button release

**Severity:** `high`

A right-button release does not guarantee that a context menu opened, yet the adapter sends a real global Escape after same-button, settings, and lifecycle releases. That keystroke can cancel an unrelated foreground operation and can become Ctrl+Esc or Alt+Esc when a modifier is physically held. Preserve the target application's normal right-button-up behavior instead of injecting keyboard input, remove the dismissal intent from the injector contract, and update the related behavior and runtime-validation documentation.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This concern requires coordinated changes across multiple current-diff regions or files, so it cannot be safely expressed as one apply-ready inline suggestion.

proposed_comments.title: Serialize setting changes with hook decisions

confidence.rationale: The runner and hook threads can deterministically interleave an old settings snapshot, EnforceEnabled, and a later stale lock write.

proposed_comments.body:
### Serialize setting changes with hook decisions

**Severity:** `high`

`set_config` updates settings on the runner thread while button events execute on the hook thread. A button-up can capture the old enabled value, `set_config` can then observe no current lock and return, and the pending button-up can finally latch using its stale snapshot. Protect settings parsing/snapshotting and engine dispatch with one synchronization boundary, and serialize deferred injection callbacks with the engine state, so disabling a button cannot be followed by a stale lock.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This concern requires coordinated changes across multiple current-diff regions or files, so it cannot be safely expressed as one apply-ready inline suggestion.

proposed_comments.title: Make the fuzz injector implement the current interface

confidence.rationale: The checked-in override has two parameters while IButtonUpInjector::InjectUp has one, leaving CountingInjector abstract and causing a compiler error.

proposed_comments.body:
### Make the fuzz injector implement the current interface

**Severity:** `high`

`IButtonUpInjector::InjectUp` takes only a `MouseButton`, so this two-parameter method does not override it and `CountingInjector` remains abstract. The fuzz project cannot compile until the fake matches the production interface.

```suggestion
        bool InjectUp(MouseButton) override
```

proposed_comments.title: Exercise each setting with the control's real step size

confidence.rationale: QuickSetValue emits one arrow press per integer while this slider changes by 100, and the current checkbox/NumberBox checks do not verify all bindings.

proposed_comments.title: Notify the policy-managed binding during refresh

confidence.rationale: InitializeEnabledValues changes the cached GPO flag, but RefreshEnabledState currently raises only the enabled-value notification.

proposed_comments.body:
### Notify the policy-managed binding during refresh

**Severity:** `medium`

Refreshing can add or retract the Mouse Button Lock policy, but only the enabled value is notified. The warning and enable-card bindings can therefore retain their previous policy-managed state. Raise the GPO property notification with the enabled-state notification.

```suggestion
            OnPropertyChanged(nameof(IsMouseButtonLockEnabled));
            OnPropertyChanged(nameof(IsMouseButtonLockEnabledGpoConfigured));
```

proposed_comments.title: Declare the policy's actual first supported release

confidence.rationale: The new module cannot be honored by PowerToys 0.99, while the current policy templates already distinguish subsequent release versions.

proposed_comments.body:
### Declare the policy's actual first supported release

**Severity:** `medium`

The new policy is marked as supported since PowerToys 0.99.0 even though that release does not contain Mouse Button Lock. Add a matching `SUPPORTED_POWERTOYS_0_102_0` definition and localized string, then point `ConfigureEnabledUtilityMouseButtonLock` at it so Group Policy Editor does not advertise the setting for unsupported releases.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This concern requires coordinated changes across multiple current-diff regions or files, so it cannot be safely expressed as one apply-ready inline suggestion.

proposed_comments.title: Format the duration through a localizable resource

confidence.rationale: The converter hardcodes the visible unit, spacing, and value order even though the PR claims all user-facing strings are localizable.

proposed_comments.body:
### Format the duration through a localizable resource

**Severity:** `medium`

This visible slider label hardcodes the unit, spacing, and value order, preventing localizers from adapting it. Load a format string using the WinUI `x:Uid` property-resource convention and format with the current culture; apply this together with the companion resource suggestion.

```suggestion
            string format = Helpers.ResourceLoaderInstance.ResourceLoader.GetString("MouseUtils_MouseButtonLock_HoldDuration/ValueFormat");
            return string.Format(CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, format, milliseconds);
```

proposed_comments.title: Add the localized duration value format

confidence.rationale: The converter fix needs a property resource whose slash-form key matches ResourceLoader lookup semantics.

proposed_comments.body:
### Add the localized duration value format

**Severity:** `medium`

Add the resource used by the converter so translations can control the displayed order and spacing. The slash in the resource name is required for `ResourceLoader.GetString` to resolve this `x:Uid` property value.

```suggestion
  <data name="MouseUtils_MouseButtonLock_HoldDuration.Description" xml:space="preserve">
    <value>How long to hold a button before it locks</value>
  </data>
  <data name="MouseUtils_MouseButtonLock_HoldDuration/ValueFormat" xml:space="preserve">
    <value>{0} ms</value>
    <comment>Format string for the hold-duration value. ms is the abbreviation for milliseconds.</comment>
  </data>
```

proposed_comments.title: Register the project as a native unit test

confidence.rationale: PowerToys native test projects use ProjectSubType=NativeUnitTestProject so the shared Build;Test path consistently discovers and executes them.

proposed_comments.body:
### Register the project as a native unit test

**Severity:** `medium`

The project currently looks like an ordinary native DLL to the shared solution test pipeline. Mark it with the same native-unit-test subtype used by the repository's other C++ MSTest projects so `Build;Test` consistently discovers the new tests.

```suggestion
    <ProjectGuid>{15f55815-dffc-4eb7-99e4-b6754a52a5c7}</ProjectGuid>
    <Keyword>Win32Proj</Keyword>
    <ProjectSubType>NativeUnitTestProject</ProjectSubType>
    <RootNamespace>MouseButtonLockUnitTests</RootNamespace>
    <ProjectName>MouseButtonLock.UnitTests</ProjectName>
```

proposed_comments.title: Release active locks for mouse side-button presses

confidence.rationale: WM_XBUTTONDOWN currently falls through even though the user-facing contract says any mouse-button press releases a held lock.

proposed_comments.body:
### Release active locks for mouse side-button presses

**Severity:** `medium`

The Settings description promises that any mouse-button press releases a lock, but side buttons arrive as `WM_XBUTTONDOWN` and currently fall through. Handle side-button down by releasing active locks while allowing the side-button event itself to continue normally, and keep the user-facing wording aligned with the supported release inputs.

proposed_comments.title: Use the serialized settings shape in DSC examples

confidence.rationale: MouseButtonLockProperties uses snake_case JSON names and BoolProperty/IntProperty wrappers, while the examples use PascalCase scalar fields that System.Text.Json ignores.

proposed_comments.body:
### Use the serialized settings shape in DSC examples

**Severity:** `medium`

The copyable DSC examples use ViewModel-style PascalCase scalar fields, but the settings resource deserializes the module's persisted JSON contract. These values are therefore ignored. Update every example to use snake_case property names with `{ value: ... }` objects, such as `lmb_lock_enabled = @{ value = $true }` in PowerShell and `hold_duration_ms: { value: 1600 }` in YAML.
